findings.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The new align-items mixin emits `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`, a vendor property that no Internet Explorer release ever implemented — IE10/11 flex alignment is `-ms-flex-align` (already emitted on line 120). The declaration is dead output duplicated to every @include site (header .contents, .small-action, badges .bullet), and it misleads the next maintainer debugging IE alignment into believing a dedicated -ms property exists and behaves there.

[ADVISORY] The mixin family's old-Gecko support is internally inconsistent: flexbox()/inline-flex()/order() emit `-moz-box`, `-moz-inline-box`, and `-moz-box-ordinal-group` (lines 102, 111, 127), but align-items() omits the matching `-moz-box-align`, so old-spec Firefox gets the container switched to box layout with no alignment rule. Pre-flexbox Firefox (<=21, which only parses the old -moz-box syntax this mixin family deliberately targets, as line 127 proves) renders .contents and .small-action as -moz-box with default stretch/packing: vertical centering is lost and .panel's `margin-left: auto` right-alignment is unspecified in the old box model — a regression from the float layout this same PR deletes, which worked in those browsers.

[ADVISORY] The header layout is made flex-only with no non-flex fallback: every display value the flexbox() mixin emits (old-spec -webkit-box/-moz-box through -ms-flexbox/-webkit-flex/flex) is unparseable in engines with zero flexbox support such as IE9 and Presto-based Opera, while the diff simultaneously deletes the `float: left` on .title and `float: right` on .panel that served those engines. In those browsers .contents falls back to plain block flow: the panel drops below the logo onto a second row, `margin-left: auto` on a width-auto block computes to 0 so the panel sits left-aligned, and `@include order(3)` is inert — the previously correct right-aligned single-row header renders broken; the artifact's own 2009-spec prefixes show it intends to support engines of exactly that era.

[BUG] The new align-items mixin omits -moz-box-align while the flexbox() mixin it is paired with emits display:-moz-box, and it instead emits -ms-align-items, a property no IE release has ever implemented. Every Firefox release that only supports the old -moz-box syntax (all of 2013 Firefox; unprefixed align-items did not land until Firefox 28) applies display:-moz-box from flexbox() but gets no box-align, so the d-header .contents, .small-action rows, and .bullet category badges render with the default box-align:stretch instead of the intended center/baseline — the site header is vertically uncentered/stretched on all pages for those users; the -ms-align-items declaration is dead weight IE silently drops. The omission is provably an enumeration gap, not a policy: the sibling order() mixin added in the same hunk does emit the -moz-box-ordinal-group counterpart.

[BUG] .panel right-alignment now relies solely on margin-left:auto, which the old flex syntaxes the new flexbox() mixin deliberately serves — 2009 -webkit-box (iOS 6/Android stock <4.4) and IE10's -ms-flexbox — do not implement, because those models distribute free space via box-pack/-ms-flex-pack, not auto margins. On IE10 and old WebKit (exactly the browsers targeted by the display:-webkit-box/-ms-flexbox lines the diff ships), the .panel containing search/login/hamburger renders immediately after the title mid-header instead of at the right edge, breaking the header on every page; the diff gives prefixed counterparts for display, align, and order but zero counterpart for the alignment primitive itself. The strongest rebuttal — 'old browsers are unsupported' — is defeated by the diff's own mixin set, which exists only to serve those browsers.

[ADVISORY] Converting .contents from floats to display:flex drops the float-drop reflow behavior without any flex-wrap, min-width, or media-query handling anywhere in the diff. On viewports narrower than logo+panel (mobile and zoomed/text-logo sites, e.g. anonymous users whose .panel carries sign-up + login + search), the nowrap flex row overflows or crushes the panel instead of stacking it below the title as the float layout did; the diff contains no flex-wrap/min-width rule to address the narrow-viewport case the old layout handled implicitly.

[ADVISORY] The .contents flex container's child-order contract is hand-distributed across two files — order(2) on .extra-info-wrapper here, order(3) on .panel in header.scss, and .title left implicitly at order 0 — with no order(1) and no documentation at the container. The next contributor adding a direct child of .contents (or reordering the header) must know to update scattered magic numbers in two stylesheets; a new element defaulting to order 0 silently renders before the extra-info wrapper and between the title, producing a visually wrong header with no compile-time or review-visible signal at header.scss where the flex container is declared. The 'each file owns its component' rebuttal fails because the sequence semantics belong to the container, not the components, and one of the three participants (title, order 0) is encoded nowhere at all.

[BUG] The `.small-action` block — the topic post-stream's action rows (closed/locked/notice messages), not header layout — is converted to flexbox and visually redesigned (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` → `0 1.5%`, deletion of `margin-top: 5px` and `padding-top: 4px`, `p { margin: 5px 0 }` → `margin: 0`), with no traceability to the stated header-layout/performance intent. Every topic's small-action rows are re-laid-out and restyled under a PR scoped and QA'd as header work, so post-stream visual regressions ship unannounced and anyone bisecting a topic-page rendering change lands on a commit whose header-only scope gave no reason to suspect this surface.

[ADVISORY] No hunk in this diff implements the 'performance' half of the stated intent — every change swaps the layout mechanism (float→flex) or retunes padding/margins/line-height, with nothing that reduces layout or paint cost and no measurement anywhere in the PR. Reviewers cannot verify the PR against its stated goal, and the performance framing lets the bundled visual changes (padding, margin, and line-height edits across four stylesheets) pass as a non-visual optimization, escaping layout-regression review by anyone testing 'the header perf fix'.

[ADVISORY] The conversion adds `align-items: center` to `.contents` but leaves the float-era `.valign-helper` rule in the same header block untouched, shipping a half-finished migration in which the legacy inline-block vertical-centering scaffolding coexists with the flex centering that replaces it. The next maintainer editing header vertical alignment must reverse-engineer which of the two coexisting mechanisms is authoritative, and the orphaned helper rule misleads anyone auditing how the header actually centers its content.

[ADVISORY] Swapping `.badge-wrapper.bullet`'s unprefixed `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline` for the new prefixed mixins silently extends flex rendering to legacy WebKit/IE on every surface the bullet badge renders (topic lists and category pages, not just the header). Users on older Safari/IE see category bullet badges across topic lists switch from the previous non-flex fallback rendering to flex baseline alignment — a visual delta on surfaces outside the header scope this PR was reviewed and QA'd under.

[ADVISORY] The hand-vendored prefix matrix in `@mixin align-items` emits `-ms-align-items`, a property no browser engine ever implemented (IE10's property is the adjacent `-ms-flex-align`), so the mixin set ships a dead declaration to every `align-items` call site and demonstrates the hand-maintained prefix enumeration is already drifting from real engine syntax. Every compiled stylesheet carries an unparseable declaration at all four `align-items` uses in this diff, and maintainers auditing IE alignment support or updating prefixes must hand-edit four parallel mixins instead of a single source of truth, with this never-shipped property as proof the matrix rots.

[BUG] `.panel` is right-aligned solely via `margin-left: auto`, but the same change activates 2009-spec flexbox (`display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box` emitted by the new `flexbox()` mixin) in which auto margins do not absorb free space (main-axis distribution requires `box-pack`), while the `float: right` fallback that previously positioned the panel is deleted in the same hunk. On 2009-spec engines still shipping at this codebase's date (Safari 6 and earlier, iOS 6, stock Android browser, Chrome 20 and earlier), `.contents` lays out as an old-spec box where `margin-left: auto` computes to 0, so the panel holding search/login/user controls clusters left next to the title and the header renders broken on exactly the legacy browsers the new prefixed mixins were added to support — and keeping `float: right` as a fallback was removed, so those engines get neither the old nor the new layout.

[ADVISORY] The `order()` mixin feeds one `$val` into two incompatible value scales: 2009-spec `box-ordinal-group` is 1-based with default 1, while modern `order` is 0-based with default 0, so the same mixin call carries different semantics per engine. The diff's `order(2)`/`order(3)` calls only render consistently because both engines' defaults sort below 2; the next caller who uses `order(0)` to force an element first gets the declaration dropped in legacy WebKit (element clamps to the default group and renders after DOM-preceding siblings) or `order(1)` (ties with the legacy default but ranks after order:0 items in modern engines), producing silently divergent header ordering per browser with no compile-time or test signal.

[ADVISORY] `align-items()` passes the modern keyword verbatim to `-ms-flex-align` (IE10) and `-webkit-box-align` (2009 spec), which use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any value outside the shared subset {center, baseline, stretch} is an invalid declaration those engines silently drop. Today's call sites happen to use only center and baseline, so the trap is invisible; the first future caller to write `align-items(flex-start)` — the single most common alignment value — gets a silent stretch fallback in IE10 and Safari 6 while modern browsers render correctly, a per-engine misalignment that no preprocessor error, lint, or test in the pipeline detects.

[ADVISORY] `-ms-align-items: $alignment` is a phantom property — no released browser has ever implemented it, and Microsoft's actual flexbox alignment property is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted two lines above in the same mixin. The declaration is inert dead code that misleads the next editor debugging IE alignment into believing a distinct `-ms-align-items` behavior exists and into copying the phantom prefix onward, while the mixin's real IE support hangs entirely on the `-ms-flex-align` line they may skip editing.

[ADVISORY] `align-items()` omits `-moz-box-align` even though every call site in this diff pairs it with `flexbox()`, which activates `display: -moz-box` (and `order()` does ship `-moz-box-ordinal-group`), so old-spec Firefox receives the flex container with none of the requested alignment. On Firefox 21 and earlier, the `.contents` header row, `.small-action` rows, and `.bullet` badges all become box containers whose children revert to the default stretch alignment, silently undoing the centering the mixin name promises; the internal inconsistency of the mixin family (order ships the -moz property, align-items drops its -moz counterpart) shows the vendor matrix was never validated end to end.

[ADVISORY] The header's flex ordering contract is split across files: the `.contents` flex container and `.panel`'s `order(3)` live in header.scss while the coupled `order(2)` for `.extra-info-wrapper` is declared in topic.scss, so the extra-info-before-panel invariant exists only as two unlinked numbers in two different stylesheets. The next editor reordering header children or renumbering the panel edits header.scss and never encounters the coupled `order(2)` in topic.scss, silently permuting the header row — a flex-container property whose value is unreachable from the file that owns the container and the rest of the ordering scheme.

[ADVISORY] The diff introduces `align-items(center)` as the header's vertical-centering mechanism while leaving the float-era `valign-helper` inline-block centering hack (the rule at line 20 plus its DOM node) in place, so two parallel mechanisms now claim the same job on the app's hottest layout path. The helper is dead weight that the next person debugging header alignment must reason about (which mechanism is actually centering the row?), and the deletion opportunity — the rule and the template element it exists for — is left unclaimed, so the vestigial hack survives into every future header refactor.

[BUG] The accepted objective (header layout performance via flexbox) silently widened into a visual redesign of topic small-action rows: `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` plus `margin-top: 5px` became `padding: 0 1.5%` (line 278), `p { margin: 5px 0 }` became `margin: 0` (line 292), and `padding-top: 4px` was deleted (line 301) — vertical spacing restyles that the float-to-flex swap does not require, since only the 4em avatar-clearing left padding had to go. Every small-action notice in every topic (topic closed/hidden/archived banners, suspension and merge notices, whisper markers) renders visibly denser than the design live before this PR; a reviewer who accepted a performance-only change ships an unreviewed restyle, and future spacing-regression bisects land on a commit labeled as pure optimization.

[BUG] The inline-flex() mixin emits `display: -ms-flexbox;` (line 112), which is IE10's block-level flexbox value, instead of `-ms-inline-flexbox`; because IE10 discards the trailing unprefixed `display: inline-flex` declaration, the mixin yields block-level layout where the pre-PR badges.css.scss code (`display: inline-flex`) fell back to plain inline flow in IE10. In IE10, `.badge-wrapper.bullet` (converted at badges.css.scss:55) becomes a block-level box, so category bullet badges in topic lists, the header, and category pickers break onto their own line instead of flowing inline with adjacent text — sitewide breakage in a then-major browser that the previous code did not exhibit.

[ADVISORY] flexbox() opts Firefox <=21 into the legacy `-moz-box` model (line 102) while align-items() emits no `-moz-box-align` counterpart (and includes the nonexistent `-ms-align-items` property at line 121), so `@include align-items(center)`, `@include order(...)`, and the `margin-left: auto` right-push (header.scss:37) are no-ops in exactly the legacy engines the prefix stack exists to serve. Users on then-current Firefox <=21 and old-WebKit builds get the header and small-action rows laid out by an old box model stripped of every alignment rule this PR's layout depends on — the search/login panel abandons the right edge and rows lose vertical centering, a regression versus the float layout this same diff deletes; if those engines are not a support target, the 2009-spec display lines should be deleted rather than half-emitted.

[BUG] This hunk adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper` and deletes the `.badge-wrapper.bullet` `margin-top: 5px` nudge — typography and vertical-position changes to the topic-page header that fall outside the accepted performance objective and that no step of the float-to-flex migration entails. On every topic page the title/category-badge block renders with different line spacing and the bullet badge sits at a different vertical offset than the design live before this PR; the restyle ships without the design sign-off it requires, hidden inside a PR reviewed as a layout-mechanism swap.

[ADVISORY] The header's visual order is now encoded as bare `order()` magic numbers split across two stylesheets — `@include order(3)` on `.panel` here, `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` in topic.scss:28 — so DOM order no longer matches render order and the numbering sequence has no single source of truth. The next contributor adding or repositioning a header section reads DOM order, assumes it drives rendering, and ships a header whose sections display out of sequence; renumbering one file silently reorders the other, and neither file hints at the cross-file dependency.

[BUG] The inline-flex() mixin emits `display: -ms-flexbox` — IE10's block-level flex value — instead of `-ms-inline-flexbox`, so IE10, which parses none of the other four display declarations (unprefixed flexbox arrives only in IE11), computes the element as a block-level flex box. Every IE10 visitor sees `.badge-wrapper.bullet` (this diff applies the mixin at badges.css.scss:55) rendered block-level — each bullet-style category badge occupies its own line at full width instead of flowing inline, breaking category display in topic lists and the header for all IE10 users.

[ADVISORY] The align-items() mixin emits -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align but omits -moz-box-align, while flexbox() and order() do emit -moz-box and -moz-box-ordinal-group, so the 2009-spec Gecko support this diff switches the header onto is half-wired and vertical centering silently no-ops in old Firefox. Firefox < 22 (which honors display:-moz-box and -moz-box-ordinal-group but supports no unprefixed align-items) gets a boxified, reordered `.contents` row in which the floats this diff deletes no longer apply and nothing aligns — a header strictly worse than the float layout being removed; the correct fix is deleting the dead 2009-spec -moz/-webkit-box lines entirely rather than completing the prefix matrix (the mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, a property that exists in no IE release, as dead output at every use site).

[ADVISORY] Converting `.contents` to an unwrapped flex row (no flex-wrap, flex items left at default min-width:auto, and no min-width:0 added anywhere in the diff) removes the float-drop reflow path that the deleted `float:left`/`float:right` pair provided. On sites whose `.title` holds a fixed-width `#site-logo` image, desktop windows or accessibility zoom levels whose effective width falls below logo-width plus the panel's min-content get the right-aligned `.panel` (login/sign-up buttons) pushed past the visible header with no second line to drop onto, hiding the login controls where the old float layout stacked the panel below the title and kept it clickable.

The diff adds legacy-prefixed properties for `display`, `align-items`, and `order`, but provides no legacy equivalent for the *right-alignment* behavior (e.g., `-webkit-box-pack` / `-ms-flex-pack`). Given the mixin explicitly targets those older flexbox models, relying solely on `margin-left:auto` risks `.panel` not aligning right under those legacy modes, altering header layout.

Within this diff there is no `flex-wrap`, `min-width`, or responsive rule added to preserve the old float “drop below when too narrow” behavior, so a narrow-viewport overflow/squish regression is a concrete, diff-grounded risk, though it can’t be definitively proven without seeing the full header markup/other CSS.

However, the key assertion that `.extra-info-wrapper` is a direct child/sibling within the `.contents` flex container (and thus that header child ordering is “hand-distributed across two files”) cannot be verified from this stylesheet-only diff because no HTML/DOM structure or shared selector context is shown linking `.extra-info-wrapper` to `.contents`. Without that, the finding’s core claim about a scattered ordering contract for the header is not provable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The `.small-action` block — the topic post-stream's action rows (closed/locked/notice messages), not header layout — is converted to flexbox and visually redesigned (`padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` → `0 1.5%`, deletion of `margin-top: 5px` and `padding-top: 4px`, `p { margin: 5px 0 }` → `margin: 0`), with no traceability to the stated header-layout/performance intent. adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly changes `.small-action` layout/styling in `topic-post.scss`: it adds `@include flexbox()` and `@include align-items(center)`, changes `.small-action-desc` padding from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, removes `margin-top: 5px` and `padding-top: 4px`, and changes nested `p` margin from `5px 0` to `0`. These are broad visual/layout changes to topic post-stream action rows, and the diff itself provides no indication they are required by the header-related changes elsewhere; however, the diff alone cannot prove this causes a functional defect, only that it expands scope and could introduce untracked visual regressions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] No hunk in this diff implements the 'performance' half of the stated intent — every change swaps the layout mechanism (float→flex) or retunes padding/margins/line-height, with nothing that reduces layout or paint cost and no measurement anywhere in the PR. Reviewers cannot verify the PR against its stated goal, and the performance framing lets the bundled visual changes (padding, margin, and line-height edits across four stylesheets) pass as a non-visual optimization, escaping layout-regression review by anyone testing 'the header perf fix'.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly replaces floats with flexbox and adjusts spacing (padding/margins/line-height) across several SCSS files, but the finding’s core claim is that this fails the PR’s “stated intent” of a performance fix and lacks measurements. The PR intent/description and any promised performance goals are not present in the diff, so reviewers cannot verify from this diff alone that there was a performance objective being missed or misrepresented.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The conversion adds `align-items: center` to `.contents` but leaves the float-era `.valign-helper` rule in the same header block untouched, shipping a half-finished migration in which the legacy inline-block vertical-centering scaffolding coexists with the flex centering that replaces it. The next maintainer editing header vertical alignment must reverse-engineer which of the two coexisting mechanisms is authoritative, and the orphaned helper rule misleads anyone auditing how the header actually centers its content.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed to use flexbox centering via `@include flexbox();` and `@include align-items(center);`, but the diff still shows the adjacent `.valign-helper { ... }` block remains present and unchanged. From the diff alone, this supports the concern that legacy vertical-alignment scaffolding is being left in place alongside the new flex-based approach, creating potential confusion/cleanup debt, even if it may not cause a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Swapping `.badge-wrapper.bullet`'s unprefixed `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline` for the new prefixed mixins silently extends flex rendering to legacy WebKit/IE on every surface the bullet badge renders (topic lists and category pages, not just the header). Users on older Safari/IE see category bullet badges across topic lists switch from the previous non-flex fallback rendering to flex baseline alignment — a visual delta on surfaces outside the header scope this PR was reviewed and QA'd under.

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `.badge-wrapper.bullet` from unprefixed `display: inline-flex; align-items: baseline;` to `@include inline-flex()` and `@include align-items(baseline)` in `badges.css.scss`. The newly added mixins in `mixins.scss` emit multiple prefixed `display`/alignment properties (e.g., `-webkit-inline-box`, `-ms-inline-flexbox`, `-webkit-box-align`). This is a global behavioral expansion for every `.badge-wrapper.bullet` usage (not just the header changes), and it can plausibly alter rendering on older engines that previously ignored `inline-flex` but now match a prefixed value. Whether it is a defect is not verifiable from the diff alone, but the scope/compat impact concern is grounded in the changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The hand-vendored prefix matrix in `@mixin align-items` emits `-ms-align-items`, a property no browser engine ever implemented (IE10's property is the adjacent `-ms-flex-align`), so the mixin set ships a dead declaration to every `align-items` call site and demonstrates the hand-maintained prefix enumeration is already drifting from real engine syntax. Every compiled stylesheet carries an unparseable declaration at all four `align-items` uses in this diff, and maintainers auditing IE alignment support or updating prefixes must hand-edit four parallel mixins instead of a single source of truth, with this never-shipped property as proof the matrix rots.
matched_golden_ids: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate explicitly states that `-ms-align-items` was never implemented and that IE10/legacy MS syntax uses `-ms-flex-align`, matching the golden issue exactly.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] `.panel` is right-aligned solely via `margin-left: auto`, but the same change activates 2009-spec flexbox (`display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box` emitted by the new `flexbox()` mixin) in which auto margins do not absorb free space (main-axis distribution requires `box-pack`), while the `float: right` fallback that previously positioned the panel is deleted in the same hunk. On 2009-spec engines still shipping at this codebase's date (Safari 6 and earlier, iOS 6, stock Android browser, Chrome 20 and earlier), `.contents` lays out as an old-spec box where `margin-left: auto` computes to 0, so the panel holding search/login/user controls clusters left next to the title and the header renders broken on exactly the legacy browsers the new prefixed mixins were added to support — and keeping `float: right` as a fallback was removed, so those engines get neither the old nor the new layout.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed from a normal block to a flex container via `@include flexbox()` (which emits `display: -webkit-box`/`-moz-box` as the first declarations), while `.panel` drops `float: right` and relies on `margin-left: auto` plus `@include order(3)` for right alignment. For old 2009-spec `-webkit-box`/`-moz-box` layouts, `order`/auto-margin main-axis distribution are not equivalent to modern flexbox behavior, so removing the float fallback can plausibly leave `.panel` no longer right-aligned in those prefixed modes that the new mixin explicitly enables.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The `order()` mixin feeds one `$val` into two incompatible value scales: 2009-spec `box-ordinal-group` is 1-based with default 1, while modern `order` is 0-based with default 0, so the same mixin call carries different semantics per engine. The diff's `order(2)`/`order(3)` calls only render consistently because both engines' defaults sort below 2; the next caller who uses `order(0)` to force an element first gets the declaration dropped in legacy WebKit (element clamps to the default group and renders after DOM-preceding siblings) or `order(1)` (ties with the legacy default but ranks after order:0 items in modern engines), producing silently divergent header ordering per browser with no compile-time or test signal.
matched_golden_ids: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core problem: legacy `-webkit/-moz-box-ordinal-group` is 1-based (default 1) while modern `order` is 0-based, so using the same `$val` can break when `$val` is 0 (or otherwise cause divergent ordering). This matches the golden issue about values needing to start at 1 and `0` causing incorrect rendering in older browsers.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `align-items()` passes the modern keyword verbatim to `-ms-flex-align` (IE10) and `-webkit-box-align` (2009 spec), which use `start`/`end` rather than `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any value outside the shared subset {center, baseline, stretch} is an invalid declaration those engines silently drop. Today's call sites happen to use only center and baseline, so the trap is invisible; the first future caller to write `align-items(flex-start)` — the single most common alignment value — gets a silent stretch fallback in IE10 and Safari 6 while modern browsers render correctly, a per-engine misalignment that no preprocessor error, lint, or test in the pipeline detects.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` that forwards `$alignment` verbatim to legacy properties like `-webkit-box-align` and `-ms-flex-align`. Those older syntaxes do not accept all modern `align-items` keywords (notably `flex-start`/`flex-end`), so a future call like `@include align-items(flex-start);` would be ignored by those engines. In this PR’s call sites (`align-items(center)` and `align-items(baseline)`), the values are within the shared valid subset, so no current behavior is provably broken, but the mixin as added is a real, diff-grounded robustness trap.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `-ms-align-items: $alignment` is a phantom property — no released browser has ever implemented it, and Microsoft's actual flexbox alignment property is `-ms-flex-align`, already emitted two lines above in the same mixin. The declaration is inert dead code that misleads the next editor debugging IE alignment into believing a distinct `-ms-align-items` behavior exists and into copying the phantom prefix onward, while the mixin's real IE support hangs entirely on the `-ms-flex-align` line they may skip editing.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin align-items($alignment)` in `mixins.scss` that emits both `-ms-flex-align: $alignment;` and `-ms-align-items: $alignment;`. The finding points out that `-ms-align-items` is not a real/used IE flexbox property and would therefore be inert and potentially misleading dead code, while IE support would rely on the already-present `-ms-flex-align` line. This is a maintainability/clarity issue introduced by the diff rather than a functional defect proven by the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] `align-items()` omits `-moz-box-align` even though every call site in this diff pairs it with `flexbox()`, which activates `display: -moz-box` (and `order()` does ship `-moz-box-ordinal-group`), so old-spec Firefox receives the flex container with none of the requested alignment. On Firefox 21 and earlier, the `.contents` header row, `.small-action` rows, and `.bullet` badges all become box containers whose children revert to the default stretch alignment, silently undoing the centering the mixin name promises; the internal inconsistency of the mixin family (order ships the -moz property, align-items drops its -moz counterpart) shows the vendor matrix was never validated end to end.

adjudication.rationale: In `mixins.scss`, `@mixin flexbox()` includes `display: -moz-box;`, but the newly added `@mixin align-items($alignment)` does not include the corresponding `-moz-box-align` property (it only has `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-*`, and unprefixed `align-items`). Since call sites in the diff (`.contents`, `.small-action`, `.bullet`) use `flexbox()` + `align-items()`, there is a diff-grounded inconsistency in vendor-prefix coverage that could affect old `-moz-box` implementations, even though whether that is a product-impacting “bug” depends on browser support targets not shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The header's flex ordering contract is split across files: the `.contents` flex container and `.panel`'s `order(3)` live in header.scss while the coupled `order(2)` for `.extra-info-wrapper` is declared in topic.scss, so the extra-info-before-panel invariant exists only as two unlinked numbers in two different stylesheets. The next editor reordering header children or renumbering the panel edits header.scss and never encounters the coupled `order(2)` in topic.scss, silently permuting the header row — a flex-container property whose value is unreachable from the file that owns the container and the rest of the ordering scheme.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `@include order(3);` added to `.panel` in `header.scss` and `@include order(2);` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` in `topic.scss`, but it does not show that `.extra-info-wrapper` is a child of the header’s `.contents` flex container or otherwise participates in the same flex layout. Without any markup or selector relationship linking these, the claim that the header’s flex ordering contract is split across files (and that it can silently permute the header row) is not verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The diff introduces `align-items(center)` as the header's vertical-centering mechanism while leaving the float-era `valign-helper` inline-block centering hack (the rule at line 20 plus its DOM node) in place, so two parallel mechanisms now claim the same job on the app's hottest layout path. The helper is dead weight that the next person debugging header alignment must reason about (which mechanism is actually centering the row?), and the deletion opportunity — the rule and the template element it exists for — is left unclaimed, so the vestigial hack survives into every future header refactor.

adjudication.rationale: In `header.scss`, `.contents` is changed to use flexbox with `@include align-items(center);` for vertical alignment, but the `.valign-helper` rule block is still present in the file (not removed in this diff). That leaves potentially redundant/legacy alignment-related CSS alongside the new flex-based mechanism, which is a maintainability/clarity issue even if it may not be a functional bug. The finding’s mention of an unchanged DOM node/template element is not verifiable from this stylesheet-only diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The accepted objective (header layout performance via flexbox) silently widened into a visual redesign of topic small-action rows: `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` plus `margin-top: 5px` became `padding: 0 1.5%` (line 278), `p { margin: 5px 0 }` became `margin: 0` (line 292), and `padding-top: 4px` was deleted (line 301) — vertical spacing restyles that the float-to-flex swap does not require, since only the 4em avatar-clearing left padding had to go. Every small-action notice in every topic (topic closed/hidden/archived banners, suspension and merge notices, whisper markers) renders visibly denser than the design live before this PR; a reviewer who accepted a performance-only change ships an unreviewed restyle, and future spacing-regression bisects land on a commit labeled as pure optimization.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly makes multiple spacing/typography changes in `.small-action` beyond the flex conversion: `.small-action-desc` changes from `padding: 0.5em 0 0.5em 4em; margin-top: 5px;` to `padding: 0 1.5%` (and removes the margin), nested `p` margins change from `5px 0` to `0`, and `padding-top: 4px` is removed from `> p`. These are real, review-relevant visual restyles/scope creep tied to the PR, but the diff alone cannot prove they are a functional defect—only that behavior/appearance will change.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The inline-flex() mixin emits `display: -ms-flexbox;` (line 112), which is IE10's block-level flexbox value, instead of `-ms-inline-flexbox`; because IE10 discards the trailing unprefixed `display: inline-flex` declaration, the mixin yields block-level layout where the pre-PR badges.css.scss code (`display: inline-flex`) fell back to plain inline flow in IE10. In IE10, `.badge-wrapper.bullet` (converted at badges.css.scss:55) becomes a block-level box, so category bullet badges in topic lists, the header, and category pickers break onto their own line instead of flowing inline with adjacent text — sitewide breakage in a then-major browser that the previous code did not exhibit.

adjudication.rationale: The diff’s new `@mixin inline-flex()` in `mixins.scss` explicitly emits `display: -ms-inline-flexbox;` (not `-ms-flexbox`). Therefore the finding’s core claim (that the mixin outputs IE10’s block-level `-ms-flexbox` and causes `.badge-wrapper.bullet` to become block-level) is not supported by what’s shown in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] flexbox() opts Firefox <=21 into the legacy `-moz-box` model (line 102) while align-items() emits no `-moz-box-align` counterpart (and includes the nonexistent `-ms-align-items` property at line 121), so `@include align-items(center)`, `@include order(...)`, and the `margin-left: auto` right-push (header.scss:37) are no-ops in exactly the legacy engines the prefix stack exists to serve. Users on then-current Firefox <=21 and old-WebKit builds get the header and small-action rows laid out by an old box model stripped of every alignment rule this PR's layout depends on — the search/login panel abandons the right edge and rows lose vertical centering, a regression versus the float layout this same diff deletes; if those engines are not a support target, the 2009-spec display lines should be deleted rather than half-emitted.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a flexbox() mixin that includes legacy 2009-spec displays like `display: -moz-box` and `display: -webkit-box`, but the new `align-items($alignment)` mixin does not emit the corresponding legacy properties (notably missing `-moz-box-align`, and it uses `-webkit-box-align` only). It also includes `-ms-align-items`, which is not a valid flexbox property. Since the PR simultaneously removes the previous float-based layout in `header.scss` and relies on `@include align-items(center)` plus `margin-left: auto`/`order(...)` for alignment and right-pushing, any engine that selects the legacy box model from the emitted `display` stack will not receive the alignment semantics the new layout depends on. This is a verifiable inconsistency introduced by the diff and can cause broken layout in those prefixed/legacy targets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] This hunk adds `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper` and deletes the `.badge-wrapper.bullet` `margin-top: 5px` nudge — typography and vertical-position changes to the topic-page header that fall outside the accepted performance objective and that no step of the float-to-flex migration entails. On every topic page the title/category-badge block renders with different line spacing and the bullet badge sits at a different vertical offset than the design live before this PR; the restyle ships without the design sign-off it requires, hidden inside a PR reviewed as a layout-mechanism swap.

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `topic.scss` does add `line-height: 1.5` to `.extra-info-wrapper` and removes the `.badge-wrapper { &.bullet { margin-top: 5px; } }` rule, which will change typography/vertical alignment of the badge/title area. This is a real, diff-grounded scope/visual change, but it’s not a clearly verifiable correctness defect from the diff alone (it’s a design/layout adjustment embedded in a flex migration).

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The header's visual order is now encoded as bare `order()` magic numbers split across two stylesheets — `@include order(3)` on `.panel` here, `@include order(2)` on `.extra-info-wrapper` in topic.scss:28 — so DOM order no longer matches render order and the numbering sequence has no single source of truth. The next contributor adding or repositioning a header section reads DOM order, assumes it drives rendering, and ships a header whose sections display out of sequence; renumbering one file silently reorders the other, and neither file hints at the cross-file dependency.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `@include order(3)` added to `.panel` in `header.scss` and `@include order(2)` added to `.extra-info-wrapper` in `topic.scss`, but the finding asserts a shared “header” visual ordering dependency across these two files. From the diff alone we cannot verify that `.extra-info-wrapper` is a flex item in the same flex container as `.panel` (or even part of the header); `order` only affects layout within a flex container, and no relevant parent flex context for `.extra-info-wrapper` is shown here. The claimed cross-file coupling and DOM-vs-render mismatch may be plausible, but it is not verifiable from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [BUG] The inline-flex() mixin emits `display: -ms-flexbox` — IE10's block-level flex value — instead of `-ms-inline-flexbox`, so IE10, which parses none of the other four display declarations (unprefixed flexbox arrives only in IE11), computes the element as a block-level flex box. Every IE10 visitor sees `.badge-wrapper.bullet` (this diff applies the mixin at badges.css.scss:55) rendered block-level — each bullet-style category badge occupies its own line at full width instead of flowing inline, breaking category display in topic lists and the header for all IE10 users.

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds an `@mixin inline-flex()` in `mixins.scss` that explicitly emits `display: -ms-inline-flexbox;` (not `-ms-flexbox`). In `badges.css.scss` the `.bullet` rule switches to `@include inline-flex();`, so the claimed IE10 block-level flex regression does not match what the mixin actually outputs in this PR.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The align-items() mixin emits -webkit-box-align and -ms-flex-align but omits -moz-box-align, while flexbox() and order() do emit -moz-box and -moz-box-ordinal-group, so the 2009-spec Gecko support this diff switches the header onto is half-wired and vertical centering silently no-ops in old Firefox. Firefox < 22 (which honors display:-moz-box and -moz-box-ordinal-group but supports no unprefixed align-items) gets a boxified, reordered `.contents` row in which the floats this diff deletes no longer apply and nothing aligns — a header strictly worse than the float layout being removed; the correct fix is deleting the dead 2009-spec -moz/-webkit-box lines entirely rather than completing the prefix matrix (the mixin also emits `-ms-align-items`, a property that exists in no IE release, as dead output at every use site).

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds flexbox-related mixins in `mixins.scss`. `flexbox()` emits `display: -moz-box` and `order()` emits `-moz-box-ordinal-group`, but `align-items($alignment)` does not emit the corresponding 2009-spec `-moz-box-align` (it only emits `-webkit-box-align`, `-webkit-align-items`, `-ms-flex-align`, `-ms-align-items`, and unprefixed `align-items`). That makes the vendor-prefix matrix internally inconsistent and could lead to missing alignment behavior in old Gecko implementations if `-moz-box` is actually used. Also, `-ms-align-items` appears to be dead/invalid output. Whether this is a user-visible “bug” depends on required browser support, which isn’t verifiable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [ADVISORY] Converting `.contents` to an unwrapped flex row (no flex-wrap, flex items left at default min-width:auto, and no min-width:0 added anywhere in the diff) removes the float-drop reflow path that the deleted `float:left`/`float:right` pair provided. On sites whose `.title` holds a fixed-width `#site-logo` image, desktop windows or accessibility zoom levels whose effective width falls below logo-width plus the panel's min-content get the right-aligned `.panel` (login/sign-up buttons) pushed past the visible header with no second line to drop onto, hiding the login controls where the old float layout stacked the panel below the title and kept it clickable.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does convert `header.scss` `.contents` to a flex container (`@include flexbox(); @include align-items(center);`) and removes the float-based layout (`.title { float:left; }` deleted; `.panel { float:right; }` deleted and replaced with `margin-left:auto` + `@include order(3)`). However, the claimed concrete failure mode (login/sign-up pushed out of view at certain widths/zoom due to fixed-width logo + min-content sizing) depends on markup/content sizing not shown in the diff (e.g., `#site-logo` width and flex item constraints). What is verifiable is that the change removes the old float “drop below” behavior and introduces a nowrap flex row without any explicit `flex-wrap` or `min-width: 0` mitigations, which is a legitimate edge-case/layout robustness concern but not provably a defect from the diff alone.
